automationNote: On 19 October a manual Run Now retry of PR #6’s matched deployment event executed the App suite on the integration preview: 32 Passed /13 Failed /76 Blocked. The ledger records this real failed PR check. Thirteen plans were corrected and independent follow-ups remain separately source-labelled in the dated triage. A fresh unattended fixing-commit → passing required check loop and production release remain unproven; the three genuine product stories retain their original sources.

stories.title: Bun gets to keep its colors.
stories.promise: A tool for shaping light should leave an artist’s paint alone.
stories.discovery: A TestSprite journey sent us to the Normal Chisel. Its setup had the wrong kind of layer. Trying the toolbar on Bun’s ordinary drawing revealed a green patch where the coat had been: surface-map colors had reached the paint.
stories.repair: The surface panel already knew that boundary. The canvas now checks it before a stroke touches pixels or history, and offers a small instruction. The corrected cloud test failed on production; a controlled replay on the fixing preview preserved the artwork and passed.
stories.scope: Exact artwork, history and refusal assertions on an explicitly checked preview origin. The automatic PR suite remains pending.

stories.title: A lock should keep its promise.
stories.promise: Some pixels are finished for today. The padlock should look after them.
stories.discovery: We asked TestSprite to select part of Bun, prove Delete worked, and bring it back with Undo. Then it selected again and locked the layer. Delete still erased it: the cloud comparison found 768 changed RGBA channels after the lock was on.
stories.repair: Drawing tools checked the lock; selection edits had another route in. The repair checks the live layer before destructive selection operations and keeps a refused floating paste available. The same exact-pixel cloud assertion now passes on the fixing preview. Bun’s selected pixels stay put.
stories.scope: Real marquee and keyboard Delete, observed lock control, unlocked sensitivity and exact Undo restoration. Controlled replay pinned the actual preview origin and full fixing source; automatic PR execution and production release remain separate.

stories.title: Every color has a way back.
stories.promise: A keyboard user should come back to the control that welcomed them in.
stories.discovery: The Colors journey moved among real palette swatches, chose foreground and background separately, then pressed Escape. The flyout closed, but focus went to a different swatches button. The same cloud check and local browser regressions reproduced it for the color wells.
stories.repair: The flyout had one fixed return address even though three controls could open it. It now remembers the actual opening button. All three opener regressions pass in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; the same strict cloud scenario now passes on the fixing preview.
stories.scope: The controlled cloud scenario opens from Primary, chooses both colors and checks exact focus return with protected artwork. Three-browser production cases separately cover Primary, Secondary and the dedicated swatches opener. Automatic PR execution and production release remain separate.
